helpers.name: reserve_function

parameters.name: file_id
parameters.description: File ID where the function will be defined (or pass file_path)

parameters.name: skip_id_naming
parameters.description: If true, skip ID embedding in name (for MCP tools, private functions excluded). Sets id_in_name=0 in database.

parameters.name: file_path
parameters.description: Project-relative path of the tracked file, instead of file_id (both given must agree)

helpers.purpose: Reserve a function ID before writing code. Include purpose, parameters, and returns — null fields make functions invisible to future sessions.
return_statements: Use returned ID for function naming: {name}_id_{id} (skip_id_naming=true for names that must stay fixed).
Fill purpose, parameters and returns now (finalize refuses nulls); they are how later sessions find this function.
result.file_path is where the function is recorded: if it is not the file you are writing, fix it now (update_function_file_location). Pass file_path instead of file_id to avoid looking IDs up.
Next: write the code → finalize_function(function_id, name, file_id)

used_by_directives.description: Reserve function ID before writing code - AI embeds ID in function name for instant lookups (function_name_id_99)
Reserve function IDs before generating function code - enables rename-proof references

implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, id, is_reserved: true, file_id, file_path} - file_path shows where the function is recorded
SQL: INSERT INTO functions (name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns, is_reserved, id_in_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1, ?) RETURNING id
Function name pattern: {name}_id_{id} (e.g., calculate_sum_id_42) unless skip_id_naming=true
If skip_id_naming=true: id_in_name=0, name stays as-is (for MCP tools that need clean names)
File named by file_id, file_path or both (resolve_file_ref); an unknown path, unknown id or disagreeing pair is refused

helpers.name: reserve_functions

parameters.name: functions
parameters.description: Array of function objects [{name, file_id | file_path, purpose, parameters, returns, skip_id_naming?}, ...]

helpers.purpose: Batch-reserve function IDs before writing multiple functions. Include purpose/parameters/returns for every function.
return_statements: Use returned IDs for function naming: {name}_id_{id} (skip_id_naming=true for names that must stay fixed).
Fill purpose, parameters and returns for EVERY function now (finalize refuses nulls); they are how later sessions find these functions.
result.functions lists each id with its file_path: any function recorded in the wrong file → update_function_file_location now. Pass file_path instead of file_id to avoid looking IDs up.
Next: write the code → finalize_functions([{function_id, name, file_id}, ...])
implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, ids: [...], functions: [{id, name, file_id, file_path}, ...]} in input order
SQL: Multiple INSERT INTO functions (name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns, is_reserved, id_in_name) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1, ?) (in transaction)
IDs correspond to functions array indices: functions[0] gets ids[0], functions[1] gets ids[1], etc.
Each item has its own skip_id_naming flag - allows mixed batch with some functions having IDs, some not
id_in_name is set to !skip_id_naming for each function individually
Each function's file is resolved from file_id, file_path or both before anything is written; one bad reference refuses the batch

helpers.name: finalize_function

parameters.name: skip_id_naming
parameters.description: If true, skip _id_XX pattern validation (for functions where ID naming was skipped during reservation)

helpers.purpose: Mark a reserved function as tracked after writing it. Triggers interaction and type-function relationship checks.
return_statements: [when:warnings] NAME CHECK warnings: a finalized name is not defined in its file's source. Rename the tracked function (update_function) or the code so they match.

[when:warnings] PARAM CHECK warnings: recorded parameters disagree with the signature (names, order, required vs default). Fix with update_function(parameters=...) or apply_audit_fixes(refresh_signature_function_ids=[...]); task completion blocks on it.

Next: record its calls to other tracked functions (add_interactions) and the tracked types it takes or returns (add_types_functions: returns only → factory, in and out → transformer, → bool/Result → validator, params only → accessor). Shortcut: audit_tracking(paths=[<file>]) → apply_audit_fixes(apply=['missing_interactions','missing_type_links']). Task completion blocks on missing edges.

used_by_directives.description: Finalize function after code written - sets is_reserved=false and updates file timestamp
Finalize function reservations after successful code generation
Finalize function reservations when updating database with new function metadata

implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, function_id: function_id, file_id: file_id}
Sets is_reserved=0, automatically calls update_file_timestamp(file_id)
SQL: UPDATE functions SET is_reserved=0, name=?, purpose=?, parameters=?, returns=? WHERE id=?
Name validation: must contain '_id_{function_id}' pattern UNLESS skip_id_naming=true
If skip_id_naming=true: skip _id_XX validation, function was reserved with id_in_name=0

helpers.name: finalize_functions

parameters.name: functions
parameters.description: Array of function objects [{function_id, name, file_id, purpose, parameters, returns, skip_id_naming?}, ...]

helpers.purpose: Batch-finalize multiple reserved functions after writing them. Triggers interaction and type-function checks for all.
return_statements: [when:warnings] NAME CHECK warnings: a finalized name is not defined in its file's source. Rename the tracked function (update_function) or the code so they match.

[when:warnings] PARAM CHECK warnings: recorded parameters disagree with a signature (names, order, required vs default). Fix with update_function(s) or apply_audit_fixes(refresh_signature_function_ids=[...]); task completion blocks on it.

Next: for EVERY function, record its calls to other tracked functions (add_interactions) and the tracked types it takes or returns (add_types_functions: returns only → factory, in and out → transformer, → bool/Result → validator, params only → accessor). Shortcut: audit_tracking(paths=[<file>]) → apply_audit_fixes(apply=['missing_interactions','missing_type_links']). Task completion blocks on missing edges.
implementation_notes: Returns {success: true, finalized_ids: [...]} confirming which IDs were finalized
Calls update_file_timestamp() once per unique file_id (not once per function)
SQL: Multiple UPDATE functions SET is_reserved=0 WHERE id=? (in transaction)
All operations succeed or all fail - no partial finalization
Each item has its own skip_id_naming flag - validation is per-item, not global
If skip_id_naming=true for an item, skip _id_XX pattern validation for that specific function

[when:notes] notes lists the notes attached to the returned function(s) as references (id, type, severity, reference_id). Read the ones relevant to your work in full with get_notes_comprehensive(note_id=X) before acting; a deferred note you resolve -> update_note(note_type='completed').

helpers.name: delete_function

parameters.name: repoint_to
parameters.description: Function ID that takes over this function's interactions (the split/move case). Edges that would become self-edges or duplicates are dropped. Every moved or dropped edge is written into the deletion note.

parameters.name: confirm_cascade
parameters.description: Delete the function's interactions with it. Without repoint_to or confirm_cascade, a function with interactions is refused and the edges are listed.

helpers.purpose: Delete a function, deciding explicitly what happens to its interactions: refused (with the edges listed) unless repoint_to moves them to the function that took over its job, or confirm_cascade removes them. Every moved or removed edge is recorded in the deletion note so it can be undone. Type relationships must be unlinked first.
helpers.error_handling: Return error if types_functions exist - requires manual unlinking first
return_statements: Ensure the function code is also removed from the file, not just the database

If refused with interactions_exist: the result lists the edges (interactions, interaction_count). Choose repoint_to=<id of the function that now does this job> (split/move), or confirm_cascade=true if the dependencies are really gone.
On success, interactions lists the edges that were moved or removed; the deletion note holds the full old rows for restoring them.

used_by_directives.description: Cascade delete all functions in file - automatically deletes interactions

implementation_notes: ERROR LOGIC: Query functions table for is_reserved WHERE id=? - if is_reserved=1, return error
ERROR RETURN (reserved): {success: false, error: 'function_reserved', message: 'Cannot delete reserved function. Use delete_reserved helper or finalize_function first'}
ERROR LOGIC: Query types_functions WHERE function_id=? - if not empty, return error with type relationships list
ERROR RETURN: {success: false, error: 'types_functions_exist', type_relationships: [{type_id, type_name, role}, ...]}
ERROR MESSAGE: 'Cannot delete function - type relationships exist. Delete or update types_functions entries first, then retry'
SUCCESS LOGIC: Only proceed if is_reserved=0 AND types_functions check returns empty
SUCCESS LOGIC: Get file_id before deletion: SELECT file_id FROM functions WHERE id=function_id
SUCCESS LOGIC: Create note entry in notes table with reason, severity, source, type, reference details
SUCCESS LOGIC: Delete function: DELETE FROM functions WHERE id=function_id
SUCCESS RETURN: {success: true, deleted_function_id: function_id, file_id: file_id}
NOTE: Interactions cascade via SQL ON DELETE CASCADE; types_functions must be manually unlinked first

helpers.name: search_functions

parameters.name: search_string
parameters.description: Free-text search over function name and purpose, one or more words (e.g. 'disk space free')

parameters.name: include_details
parameters.description: If false, omit purpose/parameters/returns for lightweight listing

parameters.name: details_only
parameters.description: If true, return only id/name + purpose/parameters/returns

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum functions returned, best matches first (default 20)

helpers.purpose: Search tracked functions by name or purpose with relevance ranking. Multi-word input is split into words; a row matches if ANY word prefix-matches ("disk space free" finds get_free_disk_space). Rows matching more words rank first. Punctuation is ignored, so no FTS syntax is needed or honored. Common stopwords (the, of, and, ...) are ignored unless the query is nothing but stopwords. Results are capped by limit; total_count reports all matches.
helpers.error_handling: Returns error if limit < 1. Returns empty list when nothing matches or input has no word characters. Falls back to per-word LIKE if the FTS5 table is missing
return_statements: If total_count exceeds the functions returned, add more specific words to the search or raise limit.
implementation_notes: Terms built by helpers/shared/fts_query.py: tokenize_search_terms -> build_fts_match_expression ('"disk"* OR "space"*')
Ranked by bm25(functions_fts, 5.0, 1.0) — name matches weigh more than purpose matches
Fallback: build_like_clause per term when functions_fts is missing (pre-migration databases)
Returns: {functions[], total_count} — total_count is the match count before limit

parameters is always a parsed list of {name, type, required, default, description, kind} whatever shape it was stored in (required null = the record does not say; legacy 'name: type = value' strings and JSON wrapped in JSON are normalized); returns is parsed JSON
